title: [Perf] Improve MLA on V1

experiments.name: mla_v1_decode_throughput
experiments.workload: DeepSeek-R1 on 8xH200, VLLM_USE_V1=1 benchmark_throughput.py, input-len 6000 output-len 1000, 50 prompts, tensor-parallel-size 8; metric is output tokens/s. Compared against the pre-change V1 MLA path.
experiments.note: Diff touches only vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/common.py: makes the rotary_emb input contiguous so the cuda kernel is correct, and reorders ops in build() to avoid GPU->CPU syncs (CPU->GPU kept). Numbers are from the PR body Performance Test (R1): the 6k-input row (865.80 vs 527.55 output tok/s, the 64% headline). Author also showed a 3k-input row that is still slightly below V0, and a DeepSeek-V2-Lite small-model ~15% case.

reported.scope: full end-to-end V1 serving throughput (benchmark_throughput, DeepSeek-R1, 6k in / 1k out, TP=8 on 8xH200), not an isolated MLA-op timing
reported.scale_short: Author's 64% is whole-run output tok/s on 8xH200; our microbench would isolate the MLA build()/rotary path. TO MAKE 1:1: on a GPU box run the same benchmark_throughput command (DeepSeek-R1, 6k/1k, TP=8) before vs after merge_sha and read output tok/s, rather than timing the op alone.
reported.scale_note: SAME unit (tok/s) but E2E vs isolated op: the reordering removes GPU->CPU syncs in MLA build, whose benefit is amplified across the full decode loop and tail latency (author noted up to 1ms p99 saved). The 64% figure is specific to the long-context (6k) regime; short-context (3k) was roughly flat / slightly worse, so the isolated-op win will not reproduce the 64% headline at every length.

environment: reported-only: author's published GPU numbers (8xH200); measured arms pending on GPU box
